_readme: Curated input for `make seed-models` (scripts/seed-models.mjs). This file is the
anti-clutter mechanism: Pioneer alone returns ~95 models including embeddings and
Gemma/Llama variants. Only what is listed here reaches core.model_library.
Scope rule: current flagship plus at most one or two tiers down. A model that a
provider has superseded comes out on the next curation pass — this is not an archive.
!! INTERNATIONAL RULE (Indy, Aug 16 2026). Where a vendor splits its service between
!! mainland China and an international arm, we price and dial the INTERNATIONAL
!! endpoint. The CN endpoint is never priced and carries unpriced_reason=cn_endpoint;
!! anyone who needs it reaches it as an OpenAI-compatible custom endpoint. This is why
!! `kimi` points at api.moonshot.ai (not .cn), `qwen` at dashscope-intl, and why
!! BytePlus rather than Volcengine/Ark/Doubao is the ByteDance name we care about.
Every provider is EITHER priced (non-empty `models`) OR carries an `unpriced_reason`
from the vocabulary below. There is no third state: a provider with neither is a
curation gap, and scripts/check_model_allowlist.py fails on it.
Two provider shapes:
source=api     the provider publishes machine-readable pricing; `models` lists
only the ids to keep and rates are pulled live at run time.
source=manual  no machine-readable feed; rates live here, hand-verified against
source_url on verified_at. The script warns when these go stale.
Rates are USD per 1,000,000 tokens; the script converts to nanos (x 1e9) for
core.model_library. `cached_input` is the cache-READ price, never cache-write.
Where a provider publishes no cache discount, cached_input equals input on purpose
— a 0 there would silently zero-rate cached reads.
`rate_basis: activation_floor` marks a row that exists only to satisfy the
UZ-PROVIDER-004 membership check (local runtimes). It is not a price and is never
billed: a local runtime is self-managed, where token cost is not charged.
Providers are keyed on nullclaw's canonical identifiers (post alias-map, see
oss/nullclaw/src/provider_names.zig): `kimi` not moonshot-cn, `xai` not grok.
!! base_url is LOAD-BEARING, never decorative. It is a CURATED field — the skeleton
!! generator no longer overwrites it — because several of our names collide with a
!! nullclaw alias resolving to a different continent than the one priced here (see
!! nullclaw_alias_collisions). Do not 'simplify' by dropping it: the failure is
!! silent — right price, wrong continent.
_generator: Provider identity, aliases, dial and display are GENERATED by
scripts/gen-provider-skeleton.mjs from the vendored NullClaw source. Do not
hand-edit them — rerun the generator after a dependency bump.
Curated by hand: base_url, source, source_url, endpoint, rate_unit,
base_url is curated: the generator supplies one for a provider it has never
seen, but never overwrites an existing one (see nullclaw_alias_collisions).
dial=native   NullClaw resolves the name; the runtime owns the endpoint.
dial=endpoint NullClaw does NOT know the name. Reachable only as an
OpenAI-compatible custom endpoint, so base_url is mandatory
and it is never offered as a credential provider id.
tiering_note: core.model_library holds ONE rate triple per (provider, model_id), but some models
double their rate above a context threshold, charging the higher rate on ALL tokens
in the request. Those rows carry "tier": "upper" and are seeded at the HIGHER rate.
Rationale: a coding agent on a real repo crosses 200k routinely, so the upper tier is
the modal case, not the edge case. Under-billing is silent and unrecoverable;
over-billing is visible and refundable. Remove the upper-tier seeding once the schema

_readme: Why a provider carries no rates. A provider has EITHER a non-empty `models` array
OR exactly one of these codes — never both, never neither (checked by
scripts/check_model_allowlist.py). `permanent` means no future curation pass will
price it; `pending` means the rate exists but could not be verified this pass.
unpriced_reasons.cn_endpoint: permanent — mainland-China endpoint. The international arm is priced instead (see the international rule in _readme); anyone who wants the CN endpoint reaches it as an OpenAI-compatible custom endpoint.
unpriced_reasons.subscription_plan: permanent — billed per seat or per plan. No per-token rate exists to charge against.
unpriced_reasons.gateway_passthrough: permanent — routes to partner infrastructure at the partner's rate. The partner is the thing to price, not the gateway.
unpriced_reasons.deployment_scoped: permanent — rates vary per customer deployment, region and commitment tier, and the provider carries no single base_url.
unpriced_reasons.credentialed_feed: pending — the vendor publishes rates only behind an authenticated endpoint; not verifiable during curation.
unpriced_reasons.no_public_rates: pending — the vendor publishes no per-token rate table at all.
unpriced_reasons.awaiting_curation: pending — newly derived from a NullClaw bump and not yet curated. The only code that is a queue rather than a decision; the next pass either prices the provider or replaces this with the reason it cannot.
unpriced_reasons.operator_hosted: permanent — runs on hardware the operator owns. No per-token price exists to charge against, and no vendor publishes one.

_readme: Provider names where OUR base_url deliberately differs from what nullclaw's
same-named alias would resolve to. base_url is curated (never regenerated), so
these survive a dependency bump; before M168 the generator overwrote both of

kimi.why_kept: `kimi` is the name users recognise; the CN/intl split is nullclaw's internal concern and should not leak into our provider dropdown.

models.note: STANDARD rate. Introductory 2.00/0.20/10.00 runs to Aug 31 2026; standard applies from Sep 1 2026. Seeded standard deliberately — see decisions.sonnet_5.
cached_input == input on purpose: OpenAI documents that this model offers NO cached-input discount.
Base tier (prompts <=200k) is 2.00/0.20/12.00; above 200k doubles on all tokens.
Also charges $1.00 per 1M tokens per HOUR of cache storage — a time-based fee with no per-mtok equivalent, not represented here.
The 2.7 generation ships ONLY in coding-specialised form — there is no plain kimi-k2.7.
Latency tier, not a capability tier: exactly 2x standard across all three columns.

litellm.note: Runs on hardware the operator owns, so no per-token price exists and no vendor publishes one. The served model cannot be enumerated either — NullClaw carries no model list for any local runtime, because the id is whatever the operator loaded. Making these activatable is a product decision about the local-runtime experience, not a curation gap: the dial target has to be gated per runner before a tenant-chosen provider id can reach a loopback port. Reasoned, not priced, until that lands.
